identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a propane-powered forklift at the Portland warehouse, recording daily pre-shift safety checks of twelve components per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7). The log documents 18 days of September 2026, with most checks passing, one defect noted (horn failure on Sep 9), and evidence that inspections were not conducted on days when the truck was operated between Sep 2 and Sep 7.
scan.freshness_note: This log is current through September 18, 2026. The supervisor review signature line is blank and undated, which is a gap.

gaps.title: Missing inspections between Sep 2 and Sep 7
gaps.description: The truck was operated on Sep 3, 4, 5, and 6 (hour meter rose from 4,819 to 4,834), but no pre-shift inspections were recorded for those days. OSHA requires inspection before each shift of use.
gaps.fix: Conduct and document pre-shift inspections for all days the truck is operated, or obtain evidence of why the truck was not used on those dates.
gaps.locator: Not in the document; inferred from hour meter notation
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Supervisor review not completed
gaps.description: The log includes a signature line for supervisor review with a blank date field. No supervisor has signed or dated the log to certify the accuracy and completeness of the record.
gaps.fix: Arrange for a supervisor to review all entries, verify completeness and accuracy, and sign and date the log.

gaps.title: Horn defect not documented as corrected
gaps.description: On Sep 9, a defect was recorded: horn not working (marked X). The log does not show when this defect was corrected, or whether the truck was taken out of service until repaired. OSHA requires not using the truck if a defect affects safety.
gaps.fix: Document the date and time the horn was repaired and the truck returned to service, or provide maintenance records showing the repair. If the truck was used after Sep 9 with a non-functioning horn, document the corrective action taken.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): do not use if a defect affects safety
gaps.locator: Page 1, Sep 9 row, Horn column and Notes column
gaps.quote: Sep 9 Day 4,847 ✓ ✓ ✓ X ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ M.C. Horn not working

scan.confidence_notes: I am highly confident in the identity, structure, and facts of this record. The three gaps are clear from the document itself: missing inspection days are inferred from the hour meter progression and explicitly noted in the document; the unsigned supervisor review is visible on page 2; and the unresolved horn defect is explicitly recorded on page 1. The defect gap is the most significant compliance issue. I cannot access the actual OSHA regulation text to confirm the exact regulatory language, but the document itself cites OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), which I understand to require pre-shift inspection before each use. The operator certifications are readable but I have not verified whether the dates shown are current or when recertification is required beyond what the document states.
